title: Engine Mount Control Solenoid
introduction:
This procedure applies to the 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW/314PS). The illustration shows the engine mount control solenoid assembly, its vacuum connections, its electrical connection and the mounting retainer. I use those connections as landmarks before loosening anything: the bracket is the anchor, and the hoses are the plumbing that needs to return to the same layout.

The removal step also contains the installation tightening specification. Keep it beside the reassembly instructions. This page covers the illustrated removal and refitting sequence; it does not supply a separate vehicle-access route or a solenoid diagnostic test.

items.name: Connection identification
items.detail: Use the illustration to identify the vacuum hose connectors, electrical connector and mounting retainer before disconnecting the assembly.

items.name: Torque wrench
items.detail: Use equipment capable of applying the retainer tightening specification stated in the removal step.

edits.text: Remove the engine mount control solenoid
NOTE: Removal steps may also include details needed during installation.
edits.why: The retainer tightening specification appears with removal, so it must remain available when the solenoid is refitted.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector and the vacuum hose connectors shown in the illustration. Remove the mounting retainer, then remove the engine mount control solenoid. During installation, tighten the retainer to 97 lb.in (11 Nm).
edits.why: The drawing distinguishes the hose connections, electrical connection and bracket attachment. The torque applies when securing the retainer during reassembly.

edits.text: Install the engine mount control solenoid

Reverse the removal sequence: position the engine mount control solenoid, install the retainer and tighten it to the specification in the removal step. Reconnect the vacuum hose connectors and the electrical connector in their illustrated locations.
edits.why: Completion restores the bracket attachment and every disconnected connection. I compare the finished connection layout with the drawing rather than relying on memory.
